answer: The draft’s defect is presenting $29.9 per share as a firm point. The peer set is 5.78, 7.12, 8.78: the 7.12 median sits inside a wide dispersion, so the read is a range, not a number. The implied EV of 4573.2, after net debt of 231.5, yields implied equity of 4341.7; against 145.2 shares that is the 29.9 per share. But that precision would hold only if the peers clustered near 7.12; they do not. The median, not the mean, is the central peer, yet a single multiple is not sufficient evidence when the peers disagree this widely. Call: there is no decision price here—29.9 is the median-supported equity value, not a cheap-or-expensive verdict.
